author: Mark Atwood
text:
The bead presents three options to strengthen the contract on update_task_per_user. All three are public-API breaking changes to TasksBackend (the bead is pre-publish but the trait is the contract surface consumers depend on), so a human-judgment qualifier applies.

Options recap:
 (a) Remove the default impl. Single-user backends opt-in with a one-line delegate. Type system catches silent-violation.
 (b) Add fn is_single_user(&self) -> bool { false }; default impl delegates only when true, else returns runtime error. Type system unchanged; runtime trip-wire instead.
 (c) Rename the default to update_task_per_user_single_user_only with stronger doc warning. No structural change; pure docs.

Recommendation: option (a). Rationale: the bead's own analysis ('type system catches the silent-spec-violation case') is the strongest argument. Cost is one-line stub in MockBackend + MemoryBackend (both already implement it explicitly today, so cost is zero — removing the default removes the trap, not the existing impls). The runtime-error path (b) trades a compile-time guarantee for a debugging surprise that may only fire after a multi-user fixture shows up. The doc-warning path (c) is the workspace-canonical 'maintainer-burden' anti-pattern: a contract enforced only by reading rustdoc is a contract that fails for any consumer who doesn't read it.

Trade-off worth flagging: option (a) means a consumer who genuinely is single-user (most reference deployments, the test jig) has to write the one-line delegate every time they implement TasksBackend. That is the desired pressure. The workspace's reference MemoryBackend (memory.rs in this crate) and MockBackend (lib.rs) already write it explicitly today.

Related cross-reference: JMAP-h47t.4 (MemoryBackend.update_object teaches consumers to skip isDraft enforcement) and JMAP-h47t.5 (MemoryBackend.query_objects silently ignores sort/filter) are parallel cases of the same anti-pattern — reference impl teaches incorrect default. They may want to be resolved as a package.

Recommendation deferred to Mark for the API-break decision.
